@@ -0,0 +1,51 @@
+# privacy
+
+The context hands the model the signed-in account's address to identify the
+user. This mod keeps that address from going out as a client's contact details.
+It holds one `tool.check` hook: a Bash, PowerShell or Monitor call whose
+input holds that address and names a User-Agent is refused. The address counts
+in any case or percent-encoded.
+
+A User-Agent is named by `USER_AGENT_WORD` (`User-Agent`, `user_agent`,
+`--user-agent`, `-UserAgent`, a prefix of those flags, `UA=`) or by `CLIENT_FLAGS`
+(`curl -A`, `wget -U`, and `-User` for PowerShell's web commands and Windows
+PowerShell's `curl` and `wget` aliases of them). These flags also count with
+PowerShell's other dashes, the en dash, em dash and horizontal bar.
+
+The refusal raises no prompt, whoever is there and whatever the permission mode.
+`REFUSAL` tells the model to run the call again without the address, or, if
+someone asked to send it, without that setting or as separate calls. A saved allow rule and
+auto mode's classifier do not clear it. A deny beneath keeps its own reason.
+
+The test is two word matches over the whole input. There is no parser, on
+purpose: it keeps the test simple. So a call that sets a User-Agent and sends
+the address elsewhere is refused, and so is one that only mentions the word
+beside the address, or real curl's `-user`, which is `-u ser`. Those false
+refusals are accepted for simplicity.
+
+This is a courtesy, not a boundary, and it covers one shape. These pass, and
+leave the machine if the line sends them:
+
+- The address with no User-Agent named: a URL, a request body, `curl -u`, a
+  `From:` header.
+- A web tool call. WebFetch and WebSearch are not checked, and neither are MCP
+  tools.
+- A value computed at run time (`$(git config user.email)`), a variable, a file
+  sent by name, a script that holds the address, a
+  client not named here, a client that sets the header in another way, such as a
+  PowerShell hashtable splatted with a `User` key, any encoding other than one pass
+  of percent-encoding, and a non-ASCII address percent-encoded.
+
+The address is the one the context hands the model, read through
+`$.session.identity()`, which answers a built-in with it. A plugin in the `user`
+tier is refused that op and is left off its chain.
+
+## What turns it off
+
+- `/plugin disable`, or `"cc-plugin-privacy@builtin": false` under
+  `enabledPlugins` in user, `--settings` or managed settings. A repository's
+  settings do not.
+- A server-side switch, read once per session.
+- A hook of an installed plugin, which sits above this one: on `tool.check` it
+  may overrule the refusal.
+- A session where no hooks module loads, where `hooks/register.ts` does not run.

@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+import { QUOTING } from './text-of.js'
+
+/**
+ * A word that says a line sets a User-Agent: its name, in a header, a variable
+ * or a script; a prefix of the flag, which the clients accept; or `UA=`.
+ */
+const USER_AGENT_WORD =
+  /user[-_]?agent|[-\u2013-\u2015]-user-(?:a(?:g[a-z]*)?)?(?![a-z-])|[-\u2013-\u2015]usera(?:g[a-z]*)?(?![a-z])|\bua\s*[:=]/i
+
+/**
+ * `-A`, `-U` and `-User` set a User-Agent only for these clients; Windows PowerShell
+ * aliases `curl` and `wget` to Invoke-WebRequest. Not `X`: `-XPATCH` sets nothing.
+ */
+const CLIENT_FLAGS: readonly (readonly [RegExp, RegExp])[] = [
+  [/\bcurl(?:ie)?\b/i, /\s[-\u2013-\u2015][a-zA-WYZ0-9#]*A/],
+  [/\bwget2?\b/i, /\s[-\u2013-\u2015][a-zA-Z0-9]*U/],
+  [
+    /\b(?:curl|wget|iwr|irm|invoke-webrequest|invoke-restmethod)\b/i,
+    /\s[-\u2013-\u2015]user(?![\w=-])/i,
+  ],
+]
+
+/**
+ * The base of a percent-encoded byte.
+ */
+const HEX_RADIX = 16
+
+/**
+ * Whether a shell call holds the account's address and names a User-Agent. Two
+ * word matches, with no reading of the line.
+ *
+ * @param text the call's input, from textOf
+ * @param email the account's address, if the session has one
+ * @returns whether the call is refused
+ */
+export function namesUserAgentWithAddress(
+  text: string,
+  email: string | undefined,
+): boolean {
+  if (email === undefined || email === '') {
+    return false
+  }
+
+  const spellings = [email, email.replace(QUOTING, '')]
+  const lowered = text.toLowerCase()
+  const decoded = text
+    .replace(/%([0-9a-fA-F]{2})/g, (_, hex: string) =>
+      String.fromCharCode(Number.parseInt(hex, HEX_RADIX)),
+    )
+    .toLowerCase()
+  const holdsAddress = spellings.some(spelling => {
+    const address = spelling.toLowerCase()
+
+    return lowered.includes(address) || decoded.includes(address)
+  })
+
+  if (!holdsAddress) {
+    return false
+  }
+
+  // The address is no User-Agent word, though `jo@x.ua:` reads like `UA:`.
+  const rest = text.replace(
+    new RegExp(
+      spellings
+        .map(spelling => spelling.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&'))
+        .join('|'),
+      'gi',
+    ),
+    ' ',
+  )
+
+  return (
+    USER_AGENT_WORD.test(rest) ||
+    CLIENT_FLAGS.some(([client, flag]) => client.test(rest) && flag.test(rest))
+  )
+}

+/**
+ * Read by the model, and by a person in the call's result. The match cannot
+ * tell where in the input the two sit, so it offers each way on.
+ */
+export const REFUSAL =
+  "This call was refused: it holds the account's email address and what looks " +
+  'like a User-Agent setting. If nobody asked to send the address, run it ' +
+  'again without it, with a generic client name. Otherwise run it again ' +
+  'without that setting, or run the two in separate calls.'

+/**
+ * The tools that run a line, the only calls this guard reads.
+ */
+export const SHELL_TOOLS: readonly string[] = ['Bash', 'Monitor', 'PowerShell']
+
+/**
+ * Where a host adds a shell tool of its own, once, before the plugin registers
+ * (register.ts reads it there). Empty as shipped.
+ */
+// module-state-allow: module-evaluation code wiring — a compiling host adds a constant tool name once before registration and never removes it
+export const INSTALLED_SHELL_TOOLS = new Set<string>()

@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+/**
+ * What the shell takes out of a line before a program reads it.
+ */
+export const QUOTING = /["'`\\]/g
+
+/**
+ * A call's input as the text that the test reads: every string in it, a list's
+ * as one line, as written and again with continued lines joined and quotes and
+ * escapes taken out, so that `cu''rl` and `"jo"@x.test` count. Both readings,
+ * since a backslash or backtick need not be either: `C:\\bin\\curl`.
+ *
+ * @param input the tool call's input
+ * @returns the text
+ */
+export function textOf(input: unknown): string {
+  if (typeof input === 'string') {
+    const plain = input
+      .replace(/[\\`]\r?\n/g, '')
+      .replace(/\$(?=["'])/g, '')
+      .replace(QUOTING, '')
+
+    return `${input}\n${plain}`
+  }
+
+  if (typeof input !== 'object' || input === null) {
+    return ''
+  }
+
+  return Object.values(input)
+    .map(textOf)
+    .join(Array.isArray(input) ? ' ' : '\n')
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@
+import type { On } from 'claude-code'
+
+import Outbound from './outbound'
+
+/**
+ * Registers the hook: a shell call that holds the account's address and names a
+ * User-Agent is refused, with no prompt. A deny beneath keeps its own reason.
+ *
+ * @param on the engine's registrar
+ */
+export function register(on: On): void {
+  const tool = [...Outbound.SHELL_TOOLS, ...Outbound.INSTALLED_SHELL_TOOLS]
+
+  on('tool.check', { tool }, async ($, e, next) => {
+    const verdict = await next(e)
+
+    if (verdict.decision === 'deny') {
+      return verdict
+    }
+
+    const text = Outbound.textOf(e.input)
+
+    if (!text.includes('@') && !text.includes('%40')) {
+      return verdict
+    }
+
+    const { email } = await $.session.identity()
+
+    return Outbound.namesUserAgentWithAddress(text, email)
+      ? { decision: 'deny', reason: Outbound.REFUSAL }
+      : verdict
+  })
+}
